speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with both psychiatric symptoms and a new movement disorder. To understand the connection, can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing, such as tremors, rigidity, or involuntary actions?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, since you were started on risperidone two months ago, I need to know if these new movements started around that time or earlier. Did your movement disorder begin immediately after starting the medication, or did it develop gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Dystonia (specifically Akathisia).

The symptoms of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. Before we confirm this, have you noticed any muscle pain, stiffness, or an urge to change your position constantly?
